title: They won the battle, then argued over the loot.
subtitle: When a shared win turns into a quarrel
then: After Badr, the Companions split into groups: some chased the enemy, some collected the goods, some guarded the Prophet ﷺ. That night {trap}each group said the spoils were theirs.{/trap} The verse took the matter out of their hands and told them to {idea}fear Allah and set right what was between them.{/idea}
now: The family project finishes and everyone remembers doing the most. The team lands the client and the credit fight starts in the group chat. The inheritance is settled and the siblings stop calling. {idea}The win was shared. The quarrel is optional.{/idea}
old: I did more than the others, so I deserve more.
new: The bond between us is worth more than any share I could win.
try: Think of one credit or share you are quietly fighting over. Let it go, and send that person a kind message.

title: A believer's heart moves when Allah is mentioned.
subtitle: Three signs of faith that is alive

row.title: a fixed label
sub: I have it or I don't

then: Right after the quarrel over spoils, the surah describes real believers. As-Suddi said a man may be about to do wrong, someone says {idea}fear Allah{/idea}, and his heart shakes and he stops. Scholars took this verse as proof that {reward}faith increases{/reward} and varies from heart to heart.
now: You are halfway through typing a sharp reply when a verse you once memorized comes back to you. You are about to fudge the expense report and the thought of Allah stops your hand. {idea}That small tremor is faith working.{/idea}
old: Faith is something I either have or don't have.
new: Faith is alive. It grows each time I let His words actually reach me.
try: Read one short verse slowly today and notice whether anything in your heart moves.

title: Faith shows up in prayer and in giving.
subtitle: The inside, made visible in two habits
then: After describing the heart, the verse turns to deeds. Qatadah said establishing prayer means {idea}keeping its times, its washing, its bowing and prostration.{/idea} Spending covers zakah and every other giving. Ibn Kathir notes that {reward}the most beloved to Allah are the most beneficial to His creation.{/reward}
now: Prayer squeezed between meetings, done fast with one eye on the phone. Payday arrives and everything is already spoken for before anyone in need crosses your mind. {idea}The verse asks for both: a prayer you actually stand in, and a hand that opens.{/idea}
old: My faith is private. What I feel inside is what counts.
new: What I feel inside is meant to show in how I pray and what I give.
try: Pick one prayer today and give it your full attention, phone in another room.

title: These are the believers in truth.
subtitle: What waits for faith that is real
then: The verse seals the list: those with these qualities are {idea}the believers in truth.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains the ranks as levels in Paradise, citing the hadith that people of the high ranks are seen {reward}like a distant star on the horizon.{/reward} Forgiveness covers their sins.
now: You feel behind. Others seem more devout, more disciplined, further along. The verse does not hand out one fixed seat. {reward}There are ranks, and forgiveness for the gaps.{/reward} You are being invited to climb, not judged for where you started.
old: I am not one of the really good ones, so why try.
new: There are many ranks, and forgiveness covers what I fall short in.
try: Choose one of the qualities in 8:2-3 and do one small act of it today.

title: Some did not want to go, and it was good.
subtitle: When what you dislike is what you need

key.label: Two reactions to a hard path

row.title: Allah knows
sub: you may dislike what is good

then: Ibn Kathir links this to the spoils: {idea}just as Allah settled the division, He settled the march.{/idea} They set out expecting a caravan, and {trap}some disliked the idea of facing an armed army.{/trap} That meeting became guidance and victory. He cites 2:216: you may dislike a thing that is good for you.
now: The transfer you did not ask for. The hospital shift you dreaded. The hard talk with your father you kept postponing. {idea}The thing you resisted most sometimes turns out to be the door.{/idea}
old: If I don't want it, it must not be good for me.
new: Allah sees the end. What I dislike today may be exactly what I need.
try: Name one thing you are avoiding because it feels heavy. Take the first small step on it today.

title: Arguing after the truth is already clear.
subtitle: Fear makes a clear path look like death

row.title: arguing
sub: you said it was a caravan

then: Some had argued: {trap}you marched us out for the caravan, you never told us there would be fighting.{/trap} Fear made the road feel like being led to death with open eyes. Others answered differently, like Al-Miqdad: {idea}we will not say what Musa's people said, go you and your Lord and fight.{/idea}
now: You already know you should apologize, or quit the habit, or call the doctor. Still you keep asking for one more opinion, one more article. {trap}Sometimes the argument is just fear wearing a lab coat.{/trap}
old: I just need a bit more clarity before I act.
new: Often it is already clear. What I need is courage, not more answers.
try: Write down one thing you already know you should do. Do the first five minutes of it.

title: You wanted the easy prize. Allah wanted more.
subtitle: Two groups, one promise, a different plan

key.label: What we wanted vs what He willed

then: Allah promised them one of two: the Quraysh caravan or the Quraysh army. {reward}They hoped for the unarmed caravan.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}Allah willed the meeting with the army,{/idea} because people only like what looks favorable, while He knows the outcomes of all things.
now: You prayed for the job with the easy commute and got the one that stretches you. You wanted the problem to just go away and instead had to face it. {idea}The prayer was answered, just not with the version you pictured.{/idea}
old: Allah answered me if I got the easy option.
new: Sometimes He answers with the harder road because it leads somewhere better.
try: Recall one prayer answered differently than you hoped. Write one good thing that came from it.

title: Truth stands, falsehood falls, whoever dislikes it.
subtitle: The purpose behind the hard meeting
then: This verse gives the reason behind choosing the army over the caravan: {idea}that the truth would be made real and falsehood shown empty,{/idea} even if those who chose wrong hated it. The small, poorly armed group was not meant to win by its own strength.
now: At work you are the one person who says the numbers are wrong. In the family, you are the only one who will not join the gossip. {idea}Being outnumbered does not make you wrong.{/idea} Stay with what is true, gently, and leave the outcome to Allah.
old: If most people are against it, maybe I should drop it.
new: Truth does not need a majority. Allah is the One who makes it stand.
try: Next time you notice a small falsehood in a conversation, correct it calmly and kindly.

title: They cried out for help, and He answered.
subtitle: A desperate prayer before the battle
then: On the day of Badr the Prophet ﷺ prayed: {idea}O Allah, I ask You for Your covenant and Your promise.{/idea} Abu Bakr held his hand and said, enough. He went out reciting that the gathering would be routed. {reward}Allah answered with a thousand angels, following one after another.{/reward}
now: The test results are late and you are pacing the hospital corridor. The rent is due and the account is short. {idea}Before you plan, before you call anyone, call on Him.{/idea} The ones who asked at Badr were answered.
old: I'll pray once I've done everything else I can.
new: Calling on Allah is the first step, not the last resort.
try: Bring one worry to Allah in your own words today, before you try to fix it.

title: The angels were good news. Victory is from Allah.
subtitle: Help as reassurance, not as the source
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}Allah could give victory without sending any angels.{/idea} He sent them, and told the believers about it, as {reward}glad tidings so their hearts would settle.{/reward} The help itself was a mercy, but the victory was His alone.
now: The good surgeon. The supportive manager. The loan that came through. You can feel grateful for each one. {idea}They are how He chose to help, not where the help comes from.{/idea}
old: If I have the right people and resources, I will be fine.
new: The people and resources are His gift. The outcome is from Him.
try: Thank one person who helped you this week, and thank Allah for sending them.

title: Sleep and rain, sent as calm before the storm.
subtitle: Small gifts that steadied hearts and feet

key.label: What He did with the rain

then: The Muslims were few and the enemy held the water. Ibn Abbas said {trap}Shaytan whispered: you claim Allah is with you, yet you pray without water.{/trap} Then came heavy rain. They drank and washed, the sand turned firm under their feet, and {reward}slumber came over them as security.{/reward}
now: The night before the exam, the interview, the operation, you finally fall asleep. The whisper says you are alone and unprepared. {reward}Sometimes calm itself is the help He sends.{/reward} Notice the small mercies before the hard day.
old: If I were really supported, I wouldn't feel this anxious.
new: Anxiety is a whisper. Calm, rest, and a steady step are gifts from Him.
try: Before sleep tonight, name one small mercy from today and thank Allah for it.

title: I am with you, so make the believers firm.
subtitle: A hidden support made known

row.title: His being with them
sub: a support they could not see

then: Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}a hidden favor that Allah made known{/idea} so the believers would be grateful. Allah told the angels He was with them and to make the believers firm, while {trap}fear entered the hearts of those who fought against the Messenger ﷺ.{/trap} The verse describes that battle, nothing beyond it.
now: You walk into the meeting where you must admit a mistake. You stand by a decision your relatives do not like. {idea}You may feel steadier than you expected.{/idea} That steadiness is not only you. Thank Him for it instead of crediting yourself.
old: When I stay firm, it is my own strength.
new: The firmness I feel in hard moments is support from Allah I cannot see.
try: Recall a time you were braver than you expected. Thank Allah for that strength.

title: Opposing Allah and His Messenger has a cost.
subtitle: Why the defeat came
then: The verse explains what happened at Badr: {trap}those who fought had set themselves against Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.{/trap} Then it widens to a principle: {idea}whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger,{/idea} Allah is severe in penalty.
now: The word is whoever, and that includes you. A command you know and quietly work around. A clear guidance you argue with because it is inconvenient. {idea}The question is not about them. It is where you stand against what you know is right.{/idea}
old: Verses like this are about other people.
new: Whoever means me too. Where am I quietly pushing against what I know?
try: Name one clear guidance you keep resisting. Take one small step toward it today.

title: This is what you chose. Taste it.
subtitle: This world's loss, and what comes after

row.title: a turning point
sub: the door is open while I live

then: This closes the scene: the defeat at Badr was something {trap}those who opposed the Messenger ﷺ were made to taste.{/trap} The verse adds that worse awaits in the next life for those who die rejecting. It is a sober statement of consequence, said while {idea}there was still time for others to turn.{/idea}
now: You read a warning like this and either skip past it or feel crushed. Neither is the point. {idea}A warning is mercy given early.{/idea} Your door is open as long as you are breathing.
old: Warnings in the Quran either don't apply to me or mean I'm doomed.
new: A warning is given while there is still time. It is an invitation to turn.
try: Ask Allah for forgiveness for one specific thing today, in your own words.

title: When it gets hard, do not turn your back.
subtitle: Staying with your people at the hardest moment
then: Ibn Kathir explains the verse as a warning against {trap}running from the battle and leaving fellow Muslims behind.{/trap} Ibn Umar and Umar both said it was first about the day of Badr. The point was loyalty: {idea}when the line holds together, each person holds a place.{/idea}
now: The group project falls apart and you go quiet in the chat. The family crisis hits and you suddenly have too much work. The team takes the blame and you let it. {idea}Your place in the line matters, especially when it is hard.{/idea}
old: When things get rough, I can quietly step back and protect myself.
new: When I step back at the hard moment, someone else carries my share.
try: Think of one person facing something hard alone. Show up for them today, even in a small way.

title: Stepping back to regroup is not running away.
subtitle: The difference between strategy and desertion
then: The verse makes room for two reasons to pull back: {idea}as a tactic, or to join another group of one's own.{/idea} Umar said, {reward}we are the troop of every Muslim.{/reward} Fleeing for any other reason was counted among the great sins, and the verse warns of Allah's anger for it.
now: Taking a week off to recover so you can keep caring for your mother is not giving up. Asking a colleague for help is not failure. {trap}Disappearing so no one can reach you is different.{/trap} Be honest with yourself about which one you are doing.
old: Any time I step back, I am letting people down.
new: Stepping back to come back stronger is wise. Vanishing on people is not.
try: If you are stretched thin, ask one person for help today instead of quietly withdrawing.

title: You threw, but it was Allah who threw.
subtitle: The hand moves, the result is His
then: On the day of Badr the Prophet ﷺ prayed humbly in his shelter, then {idea}threw a handful of sand toward the enemy.{/idea} Allah made it reach their eyes. Ibn Kathir explains that the believers were few and the others many, so {reward}the victory was not from their own power.{/reward} The trial was a favor, so they would know it and be grateful.
now: You closed the deal. The surgery went well. Your child turned out kind. It is easy to take the bow. {idea}You did your part, and Allah made it land.{/idea} Gratitude keeps success from going to your head.
old: I worked hard, so the result is mine.
new: I did the throwing. Allah made it reach. The thanks go to Him.
try: Think of your latest success. Say alhamdulillah out loud and name what Allah did in it.

title: Allah weakens the schemes against the truth.
subtitle: More good news after the victory
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {reward}more good news, on top of the victory.{/reward} Allah told the believers that the schemes of those who fought them would be {idea}weakened and brought to nothing.{/idea} The few at Badr did not need to out-plot anyone.
now: The coworker angling for your position. The rumor someone started about you. The person who seems to always be one move ahead. {idea}You do not need to scheme back.{/idea} Stay honest, do your work, and trust that crooked plans have a way of falling apart.
old: If someone is plotting against me, I have to out-plot them.
new: I don't need to scheme. Allah weakens plots, and honesty is my part.
try: If you are tempted to get back at someone, choose not to today. Ask Allah to handle it.

title: You asked for a verdict. The verdict came.
subtitle: A prayer that judged the one who prayed it

row.title: that cut family ties
sub: sure it was the other side

then: Abu Jahl prayed on the day of Badr: {trap}O Allah, whichever side cut family ties and brought what we do not know, destroy him today.{/trap} The verse answers: the verdict you asked for has come. Then it leaves a door open: {idea}if you stop, it is better for you.{/idea}
now: In a family fight you say, let Allah be the judge between us, certain the verdict will be yours. You pray for the other side to be exposed. {idea}Before asking for a ruling, ask whether you are the one in the wrong.{/idea}
old: I am so sure I'm right that I'll let Allah decide.
new: Before I ask Allah to judge between us, I should look honestly at myself.
try: In one disagreement you are in, write down one thing the other person might be right about.

title: Do not turn away while you are hearing.
subtitle: Knowing, then walking off anyway
then: After the battle scenes, the verse speaks to the believers directly. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}obey Allah and His Messenger ﷺ,{/idea} and do not turn from him {trap}after you have come to know his message.{/trap} The words in the verse are while you hear.
now: The Friday sermon lands right on your situation. You nod. By the time you reach the car, you are already on your phone and it is gone. {trap}Hearing and then turning away is its own choice.{/trap}
old: I listen to reminders. That is already something.
new: Hearing is the start. Turning away after I heard is what the verse warns against.
try: Recall the last reminder that hit home. Act on one small piece of it today.

title: Saying we heard, while not really hearing.
subtitle: The gap between nodding and listening
then: Ibn Ishaq said this refers to {trap}the hypocrites, who pretend to hear and obey while doing neither.{/trap} The believers are told not to become like them. Hearing, in this verse, means {idea}hearing that leads to doing.{/idea}
now: Your spouse asks you to stop doing that one thing. You say, I hear you. Next week, same thing. Your kid talks while you scroll and you say, mm-hm. {idea}Real hearing shows up the next day.{/idea}
old: I heard it, I agreed with it, so I listened.
new: I only truly heard it if it changes what I do.
try: Next time someone close to you speaks, put the phone face down and repeat back what they said.

title: Deaf and dumb by choice, refusing to think.
subtitle: Having ears and reason, and not using them

picture.label: What they have and don't use

then: Ibn Kathir explains these are people {trap}who do not hear the truth and do not grasp it.{/trap} Every creature follows the way it was made for, but these were made to worship Allah and refused. It is not about physical ability. It is about {idea}a mind and heart switched off by choice.{/idea}
now: There are topics where you have stopped listening. Any reminder about that habit, and you change the subject or roll your eyes. {idea}That is the small, private version of what this verse describes.{/idea} You still have time to open the door.
old: I am not like those people. I'm open-minded.
new: Everyone has a topic they refuse to hear. I should find mine.
try: Pick one reminder you usually tune out. Listen to it fully once today, without arguing back.

title: Had there been good in them, they would have heard.
subtitle: Hearing is a gift that follows a good heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains that if Allah had seen any good in them, {idea}He would have helped them understand.{/idea} Even if they had understood, {trap}they would have turned away out of stubbornness.{/trap} The problem was not missing information. It was missing intention.
now: You keep saying you'll pray more once you understand it better, read one more book, watch one more lecture. Sometimes understanding is not the gap. {idea}Wanting the good is.{/idea} Ask for that first.
old: If I just had more knowledge, I'd change.
new: Understanding comes to the heart that sincerely wants the good.
try: Make a short dua today: O Allah, put the wish for good in my heart.

title: Answer the call that gives you life.
subtitle: And know that hearts can turn

row.title: Allah
sub: between a man and his heart

row.title: later
sub: my heart will still be willing

then: Abu Sa'id bin Al-Mu'alla was praying when the Prophet ﷺ called him, and he finished first. The Prophet ﷺ cited this verse and then {reward}taught him the greatest surah, Al-Fatihah.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ often prayed: {idea}O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion.{/idea}
now: You feel moved to start praying again, to call your estranged brother, to quit the thing. The feeling is warm right now. {idea}Answer it today.{/idea} The heart that wants it now is a gift, and hearts can change.
old: I'll respond when I feel more ready.
new: The readiness I feel now is a gift. Hearts turn, so I should answer while it's here.
try: Say the dua: O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion. Then act on one good urge.

title: Some trials do not stop at the wrongdoers.
subtitle: When silence lets harm spread to everyone
then: Ibn Abbas said Allah told the believers {idea}to stop wrong from spreading among them{/idea} so the trial would not cover everyone. The Prophet ﷺ gave the parable of a ship: people below wanted to drill a hole for water. {trap}If the others let them, all would drown.{/trap} If they held their hands, all would be saved.
now: The cousin everyone knows is in trouble but no one wants to bring it up. The office habit of fudging numbers that nobody questions. The group chat joke that keeps getting meaner. {idea}You are on the same boat.{/idea} A kind, honest word can save more than one person.
old: As long as I'm not doing wrong, it's not my problem.
new: We share the boat. Gently holding back a wrong protects everyone, including me.
try: Is there one harmful thing around you that everyone ignores? Raise it gently with one person today.

title: Remember when you were few and afraid.
subtitle: Looking back to see how far He brought you
then: In Makkah the believers were {trap}few, practicing in secret, afraid of being snatched away.{/trap} Allah gave them a safe home in Madinah, with the people there sheltering and supporting them. Qatadah said: {reward}your Lord gives favors and loves to be praised, and those who thank Him are given more.{/reward}
now: The first tiny apartment. The year you could not pay the bills. The months you had no one. Now you have a steady job, a home, people. {idea}It is easy to forget the beginning.{/idea} Remembering it is how gratitude stays alive.
old: That hard time is behind me. Better not to think about it.
new: Remembering where I started shows me how much Allah has given me.
try: Write down three things you have now that you didn't have five years ago. Thank Allah for each.

title: Do not betray what you were trusted with.
subtitle: Every duty is a trust you carry
then: Ibn Kathir mentions Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah, who wrote to Quraysh warning them of a coming march. The Prophet ﷺ spared him because he had been at Badr. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}the verse is general{/idea} and betrayal includes {trap}minor and major sins and those that harm others.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said the trust is the duties Allah gave you.
now: The friend's secret you shared just once. The work laptop used for side business. The hours billed but not worked. The prayer you were trusted with and pushed aside. {idea}Each one is a trust.{/idea}
old: Betrayal is something dramatic. I'm not that kind of person.
new: Small trusts count too: secrets, time, money, and my duties to Allah.
try: Pick one trust you've been careless with lately, and make it right today.

title: Your wealth and children are a test.
subtitle: Gifts that can pull you closer or away
then: This verse follows the warning about betraying trusts. Ibn Kathir explains that Allah gives wealth and children {idea}to see who stays grateful and obedient, and who becomes absorbed in them instead of Him.{/idea} {reward}With Allah is a greater reward.{/reward}
now: Late at the office again, for the kids, you tell yourself. Skipping prayer because the baby needed you. A small lie at work to protect the bonus. {idea}Loving them is good. Letting them pull you from Allah is the test.{/idea}
old: Everything I do for my family is automatically good.
new: My family and money are a gift and a test. The question is whether they bring me closer.
try: Do one thing with your children today that also reminds you of Allah, like a short dua together.

title: Mindfulness of Allah gives you a way to tell right from wrong.
subtitle: Clarity as a gift of taqwa

row.title: a criterion
sub: truth from falsehood, a way out

then: Early scholars explained the Furqan here as {reward}a way out, salvation, help,{/reward} and Ibn Ishaq as a criterion between truth and falsehood. Ibn Kathir says the last includes the others: {idea}those who keep their duty to Allah are guided to tell the true from the false,{/idea} and given a way out of their affairs.
now: You are stuck on a decision: the job offer, the marriage proposal, the business partner. Pros and cons lists, endless advice. {idea}The verse points somewhere else.{/idea} Clean up what is between you and Allah, and the right path often becomes easier to see.
old: If I think hard enough, I'll know what's right.
new: Guarding my conduct with Allah clears my sight. Clarity is His gift.
try: Facing a decision? Drop one thing you know displeases Allah this week, and pray istikhara.

title: They planned, and Allah planned. He is the best of planners.
subtitle: The night of the plot in Makkah
then: The chiefs of Quraysh met to decide what to do with the Prophet ﷺ: imprison him, expel him, or kill him. {trap}They settled on killing him with young men from every tribe.{/trap} Jibril told the Prophet ﷺ not to sleep in his bed that night, and {idea}Allah gave him permission to migrate.{/idea}
now: Someone is working against you at work. The family has already decided about you without asking. The odds in the meeting room look stacked. {idea}They plan, and Allah plans.{/idea} Do your part honestly and leave the outcome with the best of planners.
old: When people with power gang up against me, I'm finished.
new: Their plans sit inside Allah's plan. He is the best of planners.
try: If someone is working against you, make dua for Allah to handle it, and resist plotting back.

title: We could say something like this, they boasted.
subtitle: Big talk to avoid being moved
then: When the verses were recited, some in Quraysh said {trap}we have heard, we could say the like of this, it is just tales of the ancients.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes they boasted with words, not actions. {idea}They were challenged to bring even one chapter like it, and could not.{/idea}
now: Someone shares a moving reminder and your reflex is: I've heard this before, it's the same old stuff. Dismissing is easier than being touched. {idea}Calling something old is a quick way to avoid letting it in.{/idea}
old: I've heard all this before. It's nothing new.
new: Heard before does not mean taken in. Familiar words can still change me.
try: Take a verse you know well and read its meaning slowly, as if hearing it for the first time.

title: If this is true, then punish us, they said.
subtitle: The prayer they should have made instead
then: Anas said it was Abu Jahl who prayed: {trap}O Allah, if this is the truth from You, rain stones on us.{/trap} Ibn Kathir comments on the stubbornness of it. He points out what they should have said: {idea}O Allah, if this is the truth from You, guide us to it and help us follow it.{/idea}
now: Somewhere you may be daring the truth too. If quitting this really matters, life will show me. If praying is that important, something will happen. {idea}Swap the dare for a request.{/idea} If it is true, Allah, help me follow it.
old: If this really matters, I'll wait for a sign.
new: If something might be true, the honest prayer is: guide me to it.
try: Make the dua Ibn Kathir suggests: O Allah, if this is the truth, guide me to it and help me follow it.

title: Two shelters: the Prophet ﷺ among them, and seeking forgiveness.
subtitle: One shelter remains open for us
then: Ibn Abbas said {reward}they had two shelters: the Prophet ﷺ, and their seeking forgiveness.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said Allah sent down two safeguards for his community, and when he passed, {idea}seeking forgiveness would remain with them until the Day of Resurrection.{/idea}
now: Shaytan, the hadith says, vowed to keep misleading people as long as they live. Allah answered that He would keep forgiving as long as they ask. {idea}That shelter is open on the bus, at your desk, lying awake at night.{/idea}
old: I've messed up too much for asking forgiveness to matter.
new: As long as I keep asking, He keeps forgiving. That shelter is always open.
try: Say astaghfirullah slowly ten times today, thinking of one specific thing each time.

title: Only the mindful are true guardians of the House.
subtitle: Holding a sacred place is not the same as deserving it
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Quraysh deserved punishment, yet it was held back while the Prophet ﷺ was among them. They were {trap}keeping the believers from praying at the Sacred Mosque{/trap} while claiming to be its keepers. The verse says {idea}its true guardians are only those who are mindful of Allah.{/idea}
now: You may hold a role at the mosque, a seat on a committee, a title in the family. The position is not the point. {idea}How you treat people who come to pray, learn, or ask for help is.{/idea} Never be the reason someone feels unwelcome near Allah's house.
old: My role or position makes me a guardian of this place.
new: Only taqwa makes someone a true guardian. A title doesn't.
try: Next time you are at a mosque, welcome someone you don't know, especially someone new.

title: Their prayer at the House was whistling and clapping.
subtitle: Worship emptied of meaning
then: Ibn Abbas and many others said the Arabic words mean {trap}whistling and clapping.{/trap} Ibn Abbas described Quraysh going around the Kaaba whistling and clapping their hands. {idea}They stood at the holiest place and emptied the act of meaning.{/idea}
now: Your own prayer can thin out too: rushed, mind on the grocery list, finished before you noticed you started. {idea}Not a reason to give up, a reason to slow down.{/idea} Being in the right place is the start, not the whole of it.
old: I'm at the prayer, so I'm praying.
new: Prayer is presence, not just being there. I can bring my heart back.
try: In your next prayer, pause one breath after each movement and remember who you are standing before.

title: Money spent against the truth turns into regret.
subtitle: They will spend it, then grieve it
then: After Badr, men of Quraysh who had lost family asked those with wealth in the caravan to {trap}fund another fight against the Prophet ﷺ.{/trap} They agreed. Ibn Kathir says the verse is general: {trap}wealth spent to block the path of truth becomes anguish{/trap} and brings nothing in the end.
now: Think about where your own money quietly flows: the subscription you're ashamed of, the gift meant to win someone over against another, the bets you hide. {idea}Ask of every spend: will I be glad of this later?{/idea}
old: It's my money. Where it goes doesn't say much about me.
new: Where my money goes shows what I'm working for, and some spending ends in regret.
try: Look at last month's spending. Cancel or redirect one thing you would not want to answer for.

title: So Allah may separate the bad from the good.
subtitle: Trials sort what is hidden
then: Ibn Abbas explained the sorting as {idea}showing the difference between the people of happiness and the people of misery.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to 3:179: Allah would not leave the believers as they were {idea}until He distinguished the bad from the good.{/idea} The trials of that time drew out what was in each person.
now: A crisis at work shows who covers for whom. A family illness shows who shows up. {idea}Hard times also show you to yourself.{/idea} When pressure comes, ask what it is drawing out of you.
old: Hard times are just bad luck.
new: Hard times show what is inside me. I can choose what comes out.
try: Recall your last hard week. Name one good and one bad trait it revealed in you.

title: Stop now, and the past is forgiven.
subtitle: The door that stays open even for enemies
then: Even toward those who had fought him, the Prophet ﷺ was told to say: {reward}if they stop, their past will be forgiven.{/reward} He ﷺ said, {idea}Islam erases what came before it, and repentance erases what came before it.{/idea} The warning was for those who return to the same way.
now: You carry a past you're ashamed of: the years you drank, the things you said to your parents, the money you took. You think the door shut long ago. {reward}It hasn't.{/reward} The offer in this verse was made even to people who fought the Prophet ﷺ.
old: What I did is too much to ever be wiped away.
new: If even open enemies were offered a clean slate, the offer reaches me too.
try: Tonight, sincerely repent from one past sin you still carry, and resolve not to return to it.

title: Until no one is persecuted for their faith.
subtitle: What the struggle was for, and what it was not

row.title: courage, pride, show
sub: fighting for my people or image

then: Ibn Umar was pressed to cite this verse to join a fight among Muslims. He refused, explaining it was about {trap}the time when a believer was tortured or imprisoned for his faith.{/trap} He said that is nothing like {trap}fighting to gain leadership.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said the one in Allah's cause is {idea}the one who strives so that Allah's word is highest.{/idea}
now: Your struggles are smaller: the argument at the family dinner, the online debate, the battle for a promotion. {idea}Ask what is driving you.{/idea} Pride, your side winning, looking strong? Or something you would be glad to show Allah?
old: If my cause is right, my motives don't matter.
new: The cause is not enough. Why I strive is what Allah looks at.
try: Before your next disagreement, pause and ask yourself honestly why you want to win it.

title: Allah is your protector. What an excellent helper.
subtitle: When others turn away

row.title: their approval
sub: I need them on my side

then: After offering forgiveness to those who stop, the passage closes on those who turn away anyway. The believers, still few and surrounded, are told: {reward}know that Allah is your protector, an excellent protector and an excellent helper.{/reward} {idea}Their safety did not depend on the others' choice.{/idea}
now: You made the honest effort: the apology, the invitation, the olive branch. They turned away. You feel exposed and alone. {reward}You are not without a protector.{/reward} Their answer does not decide your standing with Allah.
old: If they reject me, I'm left with nothing.
new: Whoever turns away, Allah remains my protector and helper.
try: Think of one relationship where you did your part and were refused. Hand it to Allah in dua today.

title: Even the spoils of war carried a share for others.
subtitle: Even a win carries other people's share
then: The surah returns to the question it opened with: the spoils. One fifth was set aside, with shares named for the Prophet's ﷺ relatives, orphans, the needy and the stranded traveler. The Prophet ﷺ said: {trap}hand over even the needle and the thread,{/trap} and told one man that {idea}even an arrow pulled from your own side gives you no more right to it than your brother.{/idea}
now: The bonus lands. The business has its best quarter. The house sells above asking. {idea}Before it all gets spent, remember the orphan, the neighbor who is short, the traveler stuck far from home.{/idea} Their share was written into the win.
old: I worked for this. It's all mine.
new: What I gain is not only mine. Others have a share in what Allah gives me.
try: From your next income, set aside a small portion first for someone in need, before anything else.

title: If you had planned the meeting, you would have missed it.
subtitle: Badr happened without anyone's appointment
then: Ibn Az-Zubayr explained that {trap}if they had set a date and learned the enemy's numbers, they would not have come.{/trap} Allah brought them together without plan, so that {idea}those who chose disbelief chose it after clear proof, and those who believed did so on clear proof.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds: faith is the life of the heart.
now: The best things in your life may not have been on your calendar: the stranger who became your spouse, the layoff that led to the right job. {idea}If you had seen them coming, you might have run.{/idea} Look back and notice His arranging.
old: The important things in my life happened because I planned them.
new: Many turning points came without my planning. Allah arranged them.
try: Write down one unplanned event that changed your life for the better. Thank Allah for it.

title: He showed them few in a dream, to keep your courage.
subtitle: Allah knows what a heart can carry
then: Mujahid said Allah showed the Prophet ﷺ the enemy as few in a dream. {reward}He told his Companions and their resolve grew.{/reward} Had they seen the true size, the verse says, {trap}they would have lost heart and fallen into dispute.{/trap} Allah knows what is in the chests.
now: You did not know how hard the degree, the new baby, the caregiving years would be. If you had known everything at the start, you might never have begun. {idea}Not knowing it all was a mercy.{/idea}
old: I wish I had known how hard this would be.
new: Allah showed me only what I could carry. Not knowing was a mercy.
try: Think of something hard you're in now. Focus only on today's piece of it, and ask Allah for strength for that.

title: Each side looked few to the other.
subtitle: Perception, shaped for a decree
then: Ibn Mas'ud said the enemy looked so few that {idea}he asked the man next to him, do you think they are seventy?{/idea} The man said a hundred. A captive later told them they were a thousand. Allah made each side look small to the other {trap}so the meeting would happen{/trap} and His decree would be carried out.
now: Your view of a situation is partial: the colleague you think is against you, the problem you think is tiny, the danger you think is huge. {idea}Your eyes give you a slice.{/idea} Hold your read of things a little more loosely, and return the matter to Allah.
old: I see this situation clearly. I know how it is.
new: My eyes show me a part. All matters return to Allah.
try: In one situation that worries you, list what you actually know versus what you assume.

title: In the hard moment: stand firm and remember Allah much.
subtitle: Two things to hold when pressure arrives

row.title: ask for wellbeing
sub: then be patient if it comes

then: The Prophet ﷺ once told the people: {idea}do not wish to meet the enemy, ask Allah for wellbeing,{/idea} but if you meet them, be patient. Ibn Kathir explains the verse as {reward}endurance, and never neglecting Allah's remembrance{/reward} in that moment, asking Him for help and trusting Him.
now: The diagnosis. The audit. The court date. You did not ask for this, and you should not have. Now it's here. {idea}Stay put, and keep Allah on your tongue.{/idea} Dhikr in the waiting room is the verse in your life.
old: When I'm under pressure, I don't have room for dhikr.
new: Under pressure is exactly when to remember Allah most.
try: Pick a short dhikr, like hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, and repeat it during your next stressful moment.

title: Quarreling drains your strength. Be patient together.
subtitle: How a group loses its courage
then: Ibn Kathir explains the verse as {trap}avoiding dispute with one another, which leads to defeat and failure,{/trap} so their strength, endurance and courage would not leave them. The surah began with a quarrel over spoils, and here it names the cost of quarrels: {idea}be patient, Allah is with the patient.{/idea}
now: The family business where siblings fight over every decision. The mosque committee stuck for a year. The marriage where each argument restarts the last. {trap}The energy goes into the fight, not the work.{/trap} Patience with each other is strength.
old: Arguing it out is how we get things right.
new: Constant disputes drain us. Patience with each other keeps us strong.
try: In your next disagreement with someone close, let one point go that you would usually fight for.

title: Do not set out boastfully, to be seen by people.
subtitle: Marching for applause
then: When told the caravan was safe, Abu Jahl refused to turn back: {trap}we will go to Badr, slaughter camels, drink, and have singers, so the Arabs will always talk about us.{/trap} The believers are told {idea}not to be like those who went out boastful and showing off.{/idea}
now: The charity drive planned around the photo op. The Ramadan post. The big wedding meant to impress. {trap}Doing things so people will talk.{/trap} Check why you are going out the door.
old: If people see it, at least it inspires them.
new: Good deeds done for an audience lose what makes them good.
try: Do one good deed today that no one will ever find out about.

title: Shaytan promised to stand by them, then ran.
subtitle: The friend who disappears when it counts
then: Ibn Abbas said Shaytan came in the shape of Suraqah bin Malik and told Quraysh, {trap}no one will beat you today, I am your protector.{/trap} When he saw the angels, he pulled his hand away and fled, saying {idea}I see what you do not see, I fear Allah.{/idea}
now: The voice that says just this once, nobody will know, you deserve it. It cheers you all the way to the edge. {trap}Then the consequences come and it is nowhere.{/trap} Remember who left them standing alone at Badr.
old: This urge feels like it's on my side.
new: The voice that makes wrong look good always leaves when the bill arrives.
try: Next time a whisper makes something wrong look appealing, say a'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan and walk away.

title: Their religion has fooled them, the doubters said.
subtitle: When trusting Allah looks naive to others
then: Ash-Sha'bi said some in Makkah were considering Islam, but when they saw how few the Muslims were at Badr, they said {trap}their religion has deceived them.{/trap} The verse replies: {idea}whoever relies on Allah, Allah is Mighty and Wise.{/idea}
now: You turn down the deal that involves interest, the job with the shady side income, the shortcut everyone takes. Someone smirks: you're too religious, you'll never get ahead. {idea}Trust can look foolish from the outside.{/idea}
old: If people think my faith is naive, maybe they're right.
new: Relying on Allah may look naive to others. He is Mighty and Wise.
try: Next time your choice for Allah's sake is mocked, smile, stay calm, and quietly ask Allah to make it good.

title: If you could see the moment the angels take the soul.
subtitle: The hour of death for those who rejected

row.title: far away
sub: no need to think of it

then: The verse describes the moment death comes to those who rejected, with {trap}the angels striking and announcing the punishment.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes that though it describes Badr, {idea}it is general for every disbeliever{/idea} at the time of death.
now: Every soul has that moment. It may come in a hospital bed or on an ordinary Tuesday. {idea}The point is not fear, it is preparation.{/idea} How you want to meet the angels is shaped by today's choices.
old: Death is something I'll think about when I'm older.
new: The moment of death is coming for me too. I want to meet it ready.
try: Ask yourself: if today were my last, what one thing would I fix? Fix it today.

title: This is what your own hands sent ahead.
subtitle: Allah is never unjust to His servants
then: The verse explains that the punishment is {trap}for what their hands put forward{/trap} in this life. Ibn Kathir quotes the hadith qudsi: {idea}My servants, it is your deeds I keep count of.{/idea} Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise has only himself to blame.
now: You keep sending things ahead every day: the patience with your kids, the sharp words to your mother, the sadaqah, the cheating on the timesheet. {idea}It all arrives before you do.{/idea} The good news is that today you can send ahead something better.
old: What happens to me is out of my hands.
new: My deeds go ahead of me. Allah wrongs no one.
try: Send ahead one good deed today on purpose: a charity, a call to a parent, a kind word.

title: The same pattern as Pharaoh's people.
subtitle: Denying signs, and what follows
then: Ibn Kathir explains that those who fought the Prophet ﷺ were behaving like {trap}Pharaoh's people and earlier nations who rejected the messengers.{/trap} Allah dealt with them as He deals with their like. {idea}None can resist Him or escape His grasp.{/idea}
now: Patterns repeat in a life too. You ignore the first warning sign, then the second. The same argument, the same debt, the same regret, every few years. {idea}Notice the pattern before it becomes your story.{/idea}
old: History is about other people. My life is different.
new: Ignoring signs follows a pattern. I can notice mine and break it.
try: Identify one warning sign in your life you keep ignoring. Take it seriously today.

title: Allah does not take a blessing until people change themselves.
subtitle: Blessings stay with the grateful
then: Ibn Kathir calls this a statement of Allah's justice: {idea}He does not change a favor He has given except because of evil people commit.{/idea} He cites 13:11. Pharaoh's people lost {trap}their gardens, springs, treasures and fine homes{/trap} because of what they did. They wronged themselves.
now: The marriage that was warm and became cold. The job you once thanked Allah for and now only complain about. The health you stopped caring for. {idea}Before blaming the blessing, look at what changed in you.{/idea}
old: Good things just fade over time.
new: Blessings stay while I stay grateful. Change starts within me.
try: Pick one blessing you have taken for granted. Thank Allah for it and take care of it today.

title: They denied, so they were destroyed. All were wrongdoers.
subtitle: The pattern stated a second time
then: This repeats 8:52 with a change. There, they rejected the signs of Allah. Here, {trap}they denied the signs of their Lord,{/trap} the One who raised and provided for them. Ibn Kathir notes {idea}Allah did not wrong them, they wronged themselves.{/idea} Pharaoh's people were drowned.
now: Denying a gift from a stranger is one thing. Denying the One who has fed you since birth is another. {idea}Ingratitude toward your Lord is where it starts.{/idea} Notice how many of His gifts went unnoticed today.
old: I'm not denying anything. I just don't think about it much.
new: Forgetting my Lord's gifts is the first step toward denying them.
try: Before you sleep, name five things your Lord gave you today and say alhamdulillah for each.

title: The worst creatures are those who refuse and will not believe.
subtitle: When rejection hardens into a fixed stance
then: This opens a passage about those who fought the believers and kept breaking agreements. Ibn Kathir describes them as {trap}those who do not embrace faith and break promises whenever they make one, even under oath.{/trap} The verse speaks of a stance that has {trap}hardened into refusal.{/trap}
now: There may be a corner of your own heart where you've decided: I am not changing on this, ever. The habit, the grudge, the sin you have made peace with. {idea}The danger is not the fall. It is deciding never to get up.{/idea}
old: I am who I am. Some things about me will never change.
new: Refusing ever to change is what hardens a heart. I can stay open.
try: Name one thing you have told yourself you will never change. Ask Allah to soften your heart toward it.

title: They break their pledge every time.
subtitle: Promise-breaking as a pattern
then: The verse describes people the Prophet ﷺ made agreements with who {trap}broke them every time.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}they did not fear Allah regarding any of the sins they committed.{/idea} Breaking their word was not a slip but a habit.
now: I'll pay you back next month. I'll be there on Saturday. I'll call you tonight. Then the month passes, Saturday comes and goes. {trap}Small broken promises become a pattern.{/trap} Your word is a pledge Allah witnesses.
old: It was just a casual promise. It doesn't really count.
new: Every promise counts. Keeping my word is part of fearing Allah.
try: Think of one promise you have not kept. Keep it today, or apologize and set a real date.

title: So that those behind them might take a lesson.
subtitle: Consequences that teach others
then: This verse addressed the Prophet ﷺ about those who kept breaking treaties in war. The aim, it says, was {idea}that those behind them would take heed.{/idea} As-Suddi said: {idea}so they would be careful not to break treaties{/idea} and meet the same end.
now: Your kids watch what happens when you lie to the landlord. Your juniors watch what happens when you cut a corner. {idea}Consequences teach the people around you.{/idea} Let them learn from what you got right, and from how you made right what you got wrong.
old: My choices only affect me.
new: People behind me learn from what my choices lead to.
try: Think of one person who watches you closely. Do one thing today you'd want them to copy.

title: Even with an enemy, never betray. Be open and equal.
subtitle: Honesty that holds even in conflict
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah's dislike of treachery {idea}includes treachery against disbelievers.{/idea} Mu'awiyah once moved his army close to Roman lands while a peace treaty still stood, planning to attack the moment it ended. {trap}Amr bin Anbasah called out: be honest, stay away from betrayal,{/trap} and quoted the Prophet ﷺ. Mu'awiyah turned back.
now: The business partner you suspect is cheating you. The ex in a custody dispute. The neighbor you are feuding with. {trap}The temptation is to betray first.{/trap} The verse says: be open, say it plainly, keep your hands clean. Allah does not love traitors.
old: If I suspect someone will cheat me, I can get them first.
new: Even with someone I don't trust, I stay honest and say things openly.
try: In one tense relationship, choose honesty today: say clearly what you plan instead of acting behind their back.

title: No one outruns Allah.
subtitle: Getting away with it is an illusion
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}do not think they have escaped Us{/trap} or that We are unable to reach them. {idea}They are within Our power and in the grasp of Our will.{/idea} He links it to 29:4: do those who do evil think they can outrun Us?
now: The thing you did that nobody found out about. The money that never got traced. The lie that held. {idea}It feels like you got away with it.{/idea} That feeling is the reason to turn back now, while repentance is still open.
old: Nobody found out, so it's behind me.
new: No one outruns Allah. What I hid is still mine to make right.
try: Think of one wrong you got away with. Make it right if you can, and ask Allah's forgiveness today.

title: Prepare what you can. What you spend for Allah returns.
subtitle: Doing your part, then trusting
then: Ibn Kathir explains the verse as preparing {idea}as much as possible, according to what is affordable and available.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said of three people keeping horses: {trap}one keeps it for pride and show, and it is a burden on him.{/trap} The verse ends: {reward}whatever you spend in Allah's cause will be repaid in full.{/reward}
now: You pray for the job but haven't updated your CV. You want to raise strong kids but haven't read with them in weeks. {idea}The verse asks you to prepare what you can.{/idea} Effort is not the opposite of trust. It is how trust looks in practice.
old: If I trust Allah enough, I don't need to prepare.
new: I prepare all I can, and trust Allah with what I can't.
try: Pick one thing you've been praying about. Take one practical step to prepare for it today.

title: If they lean toward peace, lean toward it too.
subtitle: Taking the open hand, and trusting Allah

key.label: What to do with an offer of peace

then: Ibn Kathir notes that when Quraysh sought peace at Hudaybiyah, {idea}the Prophet ﷺ accepted it, and other terms they brought.{/idea} Ali reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}there will be disputes after me, so if you can end them in peace, do so.{/reward}
now: Your brother texts after a year of silence: can we talk? Your colleague offers coffee after the fight. {idea}The part of you that wants to keep score will look for reasons to refuse.{/idea} Lean toward it. Trust Allah with the rest.
old: If I accept their peace too quickly, I'll look weak.
new: When someone leans toward peace, I lean too, and leave the rest with Allah.
try: If someone has reached out to make peace, reply today with something warm.

title: If they mean to deceive you, Allah is enough for you.
subtitle: Choosing peace without fearing the trick
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the believers were told to accept peace and trust Allah, because {reward}Allah would suffice for them and help them{/reward} even if the other side offered peace {trap}as a trick to regroup.{/trap} He reminded them that He had already supported the Prophet ﷺ with His help and with the believers.
now: You're afraid that if you forgive, they'll hurt you again. That if you're generous, you'll be used. {idea}Act rightly, and leave the risk with Allah.{/idea} He is enough for the one who does what is right.
old: If I'm generous and they take advantage, I lose.
new: If I do right and they deceive me, Allah is still enough for me.
try: Make the dua hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me, about one person you are wary of.

title: All the money on earth could not unite those hearts.
subtitle: Only Allah joins hearts together
then: Before Islam the two Ansar tribes, {trap}Aws and Khazraj, had fought many wars{/trap} with endless reasons for unrest. Allah ended that with faith. After Hunayn the Prophet ﷺ asked the Ansar: {idea}were you not divided, and Allah united you through me?{/idea} They answered: the favor is from Allah and His Messenger.
now: The family that hasn't sat at one table in years. The two friends who stopped speaking. You have tried gifts, mediators, long messages. {idea}Hearts are His to join.{/idea} Keep doing your part, and ask Him for what you cannot buy.
old: If I try hard enough, I can fix this relationship myself.
new: I do my part, but only Allah can truly join hearts.
try: Pick one broken relationship and make dua today, by name, for Allah to join your hearts.

title: Allah is enough for you, and for those who follow you.
subtitle: Sufficiency that extends to the followers
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {reward}Allah will suffice, aid and support the believers{/reward} even when their enemies are numerous and well supplied, while they are few. The promise reaches beyond the Prophet ﷺ to {idea}whoever follows him.{/idea}
now: You count what you have: savings, contacts, health, qualifications. It never feels like enough. {reward}Allah is enough for those who follow His Messenger ﷺ.{/reward} Not instead of effort, but under all of it.
old: I need more resources before I can feel secure.
new: Following the Prophet ﷺ, I have Allah, and He is enough.
try: When worry about having enough comes today, say hasbiyallah and name one way Allah has provided.

title: Twenty who are steadfast can overcome two hundred.
subtitle: Patience multiplies a small number
then: At Badr the Prophet ﷺ told his Companions: {reward}rise toward a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth.{/reward} Umayr bin Al-Humam said, excellent, excellent, hoping to be among its people. The verse promised that {idea}twenty who were steadfast would overcome two hundred.{/idea}
now: You are the only one in your office who prays. The only one in your family trying to quit smoking. The few volunteers keeping the food bank open. {idea}Being few is not the same as being weak.{/idea} Steady, patient people carry far more than their number.
old: There are too few of us to make a difference.
new: A few patient, steady people can do what crowds cannot.
try: Find one other person working toward the same good as you, and encourage them today.

title: Now Allah has lightened it, knowing there is weakness in you.
subtitle: A load adjusted to what people can bear
then: Ibn Abbas said the earlier ratio {trap}became difficult for the Muslims.{/trap} Then came this verse: {reward}now Allah has lightened it for you, for He knows there is weakness in you.{/reward} The load was eased to match what they could carry, and the verse ends: Allah is with the patient.
now: You set yourself a plan: pray every night, read a juz a day, never lose your temper. You fell short and want to give up entirely. {idea}Allah knows your weakness and still asks for what you can do.{/idea} Lighten the plan, don't drop it.
old: If I can't do the full amount, there's no point.
new: Allah knows my weakness. A smaller, steady amount is still welcome.
try: Take one goal you've been failing at. Cut it to a size you can actually keep, and start today.

title: You want this world's gain. Allah wants the Hereafter for you.
subtitle: The question of the captives at Badr
then: After Badr the Prophet ﷺ asked his Companions about the captives, saying {idea}only yesterday they were your brothers.{/idea} Umar advised one course, Abu Bakr advised pardon in exchange for ransom, and the Prophet ﷺ accepted ransom. The verse came: {trap}you desire the goods of this world,{/trap} {idea}but Allah desires the Hereafter.{/idea}
now: A decision at work: the option that pays more now, or the one you'd be proud of before Allah. The weekend: the extra shift, or the visit to your aging mother. {idea}Ask which want is leading.{/idea}
old: Taking the gain in front of me is just being practical.
new: Allah wants the lasting good for me. I can let that lead my choices.
try: In one choice today, ask which option you'd prefer on the Day you meet Allah, and pick it.

title: Were it not for a prior decree from Allah.
subtitle: Mercy that was written before the mistake
then: Ibn Abbas and many others explained the prior decree as {reward}Allah having already written that spoils would be made lawful for this community.{/reward} Without it, {trap}a great punishment would have touched them for what they took.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said he was given things no prophet before him was given.
now: You look back at a decision that could have gone badly: the drive home tired, the investment you didn't check, the words you almost said. {reward}You were spared before you knew you needed it.{/reward} That is mercy written ahead of time.
old: It turned out fine, so I must have been right.
new: Sometimes I was spared not because I was right, but because Allah's mercy came first.
try: Recall a close call in your life. Thank Allah today for the mercy you didn't see at the time.

title: Enjoy what is lawful and good, and keep mindful of Allah.
subtitle: After the warning, permission and forgiveness

key.label: How to hold what is lawful

then: After the stern words of the last two verses, Allah tells them {reward}to eat of what they had gained, lawful and good,{/reward} and {idea}to stay mindful of Him.{/idea} Abu Hurayrah said this is because spoils had never been made lawful for anyone before them. The verse ends: Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
now: You earned your salary honestly, and still feel strange enjoying it. Or you enjoy it so much you forget who gave it. {idea}The verse finds the middle.{/idea} Enjoy what is lawful, gratefully, with Allah in mind.
old: Enjoying good things feels a bit unspiritual.
new: Enjoying the lawful with gratitude and taqwa is what Allah invites.
try: Enjoy one good, lawful thing today slowly, and thank Allah for it out loud.

title: If there is good in your hearts, He will give you better.
subtitle: Hope offered to the captives
then: Al-Abbas, the Prophet's ﷺ uncle, was among the captives and had to pay ransom. Ibn Kathir reports that {trap}he lost twenty uwqiyah,{/trap} and later said: {reward}after I became Muslim, Allah gave me twenty servants in their place, and I hope for His forgiveness.{/reward} The night after Badr, the Prophet ﷺ could not sleep until his uncle's bonds were loosened.
now: The job you lost, the money that disappeared in a bad deal, the plan that fell through. {reward}Allah looks at your heart, not just your account.{/reward} If there is good there, what He gives in return can be better than what was taken.
old: What I lost is gone. Nothing can replace it.
new: If Allah finds good in my heart, He can give me better than what I lost.
try: Think of one recent loss. Ask Allah sincerely to replace it with something better.

title: If they plan to betray you, Allah already knows.
subtitle: Words said and what is in the heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains: if they intend to betray you, {trap}contrary to what they declare in words,{/trap} they already betrayed Allah before Badr. {idea}Allah knows what they do and is Wise in what He decides.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ was not asked to read hearts.
now: You suspect someone's kindness is fake: the in-law, the coworker, the new friend. You replay their words, hunting for the trick. {idea}You are not asked to read hearts.{/idea} Act fairly on what you see, and leave the rest to the All-Knowing.
old: I need to figure out what everyone is really thinking.
new: I deal with what I can see. Allah knows what is hidden.
try: Next time you catch yourself guessing someone's hidden motive, stop and give them the benefit of the doubt.

title: Those who left everything and those who took them in.
subtitle: The Muhajirin and the Ansar, allies to one another

row.title: allies
sub: each more right to the other

then: The Muhajirin {idea}left their homes and estates for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.{/idea} The Ansar of Madinah {reward}took them into their own homes and shared their wealth.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ paired them as brothers. The verse also tells them to help believers far away who ask for aid, {idea}without breaking any treaty they had made.{/idea}
now: The family that just arrived in your city knowing no one. The student far from home during Ramadan. The colleague who moved here alone. {idea}You can be someone's Ansar.{/idea} A meal, a lift, a spare room for a week.
old: Newcomers will find their own way. It's not my responsibility.
new: Taking in those who left home is how strangers become brothers and sisters.
try: Invite someone new to your area, or far from family, for a meal this week.

title: If you do not stand by one another, corruption spreads.
subtitle: What happens when the good stop supporting each other
then: After describing the bond among believers, the verse notes that {trap}those who opposed them supported one another.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that if the believers {idea}did not stay loyal to each other,{/idea} confusion and widespread trial would follow. The concern was the community holding together in that early time.
now: The honest colleague who gets isolated while the cliquey ones protect each other. The friend trying to stay sober who gets no backup. {idea}People doing wrong often stick together. People doing right often leave each other alone.{/idea} Be the support.
old: As long as I'm doing good myself, that's enough.
new: Good people need to stand by each other, or wrong fills the gap.
try: Message one person who is trying to do the right thing and tell them you're with them.

title: They are the believers in truth.
subtitle: The surah ends where it began

row.title: love and follow them
sub: a person is with whom he loves

then: Ibn Kathir notes the surah {idea}affirms their faith just as at its beginning,{/idea} echoing 8:4: these are the believers in truth. The Prophet ﷺ said, in a hadith with many chains: {reward}a person will be with those he loves.{/reward}
now: You weren't at Badr. You didn't leave Makkah or open your home in Madinah. {reward}You can still love them and walk their way.{/reward} Read about them, give like the Ansar, hold firm like the Muhajirin, in the small daily ways your life allows.
old: The best generation is gone. I can only admire them from far away.
new: Loving them and following their way, I can hope to be with them.
try: Read one short story about a Companion today and copy one thing they did.

title: Those who came later and strove with you are of you.
subtitle: Late arrivals belong, and family ties keep their right

row.title: too late to belong
sub: the first ones got it all

then: The surah ends by welcoming {idea}those who believed afterward, emigrated, and strove alongside the first believers: they are of you.{/idea} It then states that {reward}relatives by blood are nearer to one another in Allah's decree,{/reward} which Ibn Abbas and others said replaced the early inheritance between paired brothers.
now: You came to practice late: after years away, after university, after your first child. You feel like you missed the start. {idea}The verse says: you are of them.{/idea} And while you embrace your new brothers and sisters, don't neglect your own family.
old: I came to faith too late to really belong.
new: Those who come later and strive are fully counted. And my family still has its right.
try: Call one relative you've drifted from today, and welcome one newcomer at the mosque this week.
